title: Big Change: Power Plants May Soon Pollute More
summary:
Imagine a giant factory with a chimney. Right now, rules say that chimney can't puff out too much dirty air. But soon, that could change.

The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is a government group that takes care of the environment. It wants to get rid of rules that limit greenhouse gases from power plants. Greenhouse gases are gases that trap heat and make the Earth warmer. These plants burn coal and natural gas to make electricity for our homes and schools.

EPA boss Lee Zeldin says the old rules cost too much money. He says removing them will "unleash" American energy. President Donald Trump has called climate change "the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world." He wants to make it easier to make electricity.

But many people are worried. Vickie Patton from the Environmental Defense Fund says the change is dangerous. She says families are already facing record-breaking heat, bigger floods, and storms. Power plants make about one-quarter of the country's climate pollution. That's a lot! The rules could have prevented 30,000 deaths every year and saved $275 billion. That's like saving enough money to buy every kid in America a laptop!

Environmental groups promise to fight this in court. So this story is far from over.
why_it_matters: These air rules help decide what kids breathe and how hot summers get, so the choices made now will shape the world you grow up in.

background_read: The Environmental Protection Agency (the U.S. government group that watches over air, water, and land) was created back in 1970, after America's rivers and skies had become very polluted.
The EPA's boss, Lee Zeldin (the EPA administrator since 2025), was picked by President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025).
Rules about pollution from power plants have gone back and forth for years — one president makes them stronger, the next makes them weaker, and courts often decide who is right.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), led by its boss Lee Zeldin, and President Donald Trump want to remove limits on greenhouse gases from power plants.
WHAT: The EPA wants to get rid of the rules that limit greenhouse gases from power plants that burn coal and natural gas, and environmental groups promise to fight this in court.
WHERE: In the United States, where power plants make about one-quarter of the country's climate pollution.

WHY: Supporters say the old rules cost too much money and ending them will unleash American energy; critics like Vickie Patton of the Environmental Defense Fund say the change is dangerous as families already face record-breaking heat, bigger floods and storms.

perspectives.description: They say the old rules cost too much money, so making electricity could get cheaper and America could make more of its own energy without extra paperwork.
Groups like the Environmental Defense Fund say the change is dangerous because families are already facing record-breaking heat, bigger floods and storms, and dirtier air can make people sick.
They point out that pollution rules have changed many times with new presidents, so the real answer may come from judges in court rather than from either side right now.
